title: Grammar: Grammar
subtitle: A2 · Unit 2: What happened this week?

steps.title: Grammar
steps.body: For the verbs practised in this lesson, build the passé composé with the present of avoir plus a past participle. Most French verbs use avoir, but some common verbs use être; Unit 3 introduces a starter set. For a regular -er verb such as réserver, remove -er and add -é. The subject still controls the form of avoir.

steps.title: A finished action: avoir + a regular past participle
Grammar
steps.body:
• Look for the time clue, then ask: what finished action happened?
• Keep avoir in the present: j'ai, tu as, elle a. Put the main action in the past participle.
• Most regular -er participles end in -é. Hear the difference between je réserve (now) and j'ai réservé (finished).
• Do not add -s to the past participle with avoir just because the subject is plural: elles ont réservé.

steps.explain: Use present avoir plus the past participle réservé: nous avons réservé.
With elle, use a plus terminé.
The order is subject + avoir + past participle: vous avez confirmé.

steps.prompt: Which sentence describes a finished action?
steps.explain: Ont étudié is a completed past action; the other sentences are present or future.
